channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: South Korean Won: Strength extends on intervention talk against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank economists highlight ongoing Korean Won (KRW) appreciation against the Dollar. USD/KRW slipped 0.1% to 1,430, extending declines from earlier in the week.

item.title: Forex Today: Gold surges above $4,240 as US labor data crumbles
item.description: Metals were the biggest earners of the day on Wednesday, with Gold surging more than 4% to trade near $4,247 per troy ounce and Silver rallying almost 5% toward $62.20 amid a softer-than-expected US labor market report, with a slowdown in private hiring.

item.title: Fed Cook backs hold but warns rate hike possible if disinflation stalls
item.description: Fed Governor Lisa Cook said she supported leaving rates unchanged at the last Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, as she awaits more data. She added that inflation risks outweigh job market risks, while reaffirming her full commitment to restoring price stability.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Break of 1.2790 may unlock further gains – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD was broadly flat on Tuesday, with SGD NEER trading 1.5–2.0% above its mid-point, implying a 1.2773–1.2837 range. Intraday, they expect consolidation between 1.2805 and 1.2840.

item.title: Mexican Peso extends nine-day gains as Gulf War de-escalates
item.description: The Mexican Peso extends its gains for the ninth consecutive day on Wednesday, as the US Dollar remains on the back foot amid softer-than-expected US jobs data ahead of the crucial Nonfarm Payrolls report. The USD/MXN trades at 17.24, down 0.10%.

item.title: Japan: Passive foreign interest limits upside – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that foreign demand for Japanese equities remains subdued compared with interest in JPY and JGBs.

item.title: Asian FX: Repricing risk as policymakers resist weakness – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee argues that Asian currencies may face repricing risk as global policymakers increasingly resist competitive depreciation.

item.title: Euro advances as US labor data disappoints
item.description: EUR/USD trades on the front foot near 1.1560 on Wednesday, adding around 0.2% as a weak United States (US) labor market report undermines the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG skyrockets above $60, tests 50-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price surges more than 4% on Wednesday as the Greenback remains on the back foot due to softer-than-expected jobs and data, though the fall was capped as business activity in the services sector continued to expand.

item.title: British Pound: Range trade holds ahead of Q2 GDP against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the British Pound (GBP) is slightly firmer versus the US Dollar (USD), with modestly better PMIs but a fading fundamental backdrop as 2-year spreads give back gains since late June.

item.title: Gold rallies as Iran-US deal seems closer ahead of NFP
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price surges to its highest level in nearly seven weeks, gaining nearly 3.80% on Wednesday as the Greenback loses ground and US Treasury yields fail to gain traction. The XAU/USD pair trades at $4,232, its highest level since June 18, after bouncing off daily lows of $4,065.

item.title: WTI holds near three-week low as traders await Hormuz agreement
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Crude Oil remains under pressure on Wednesday but struggles to attract fresh selling as traders await confirmation that commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz will resume. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $74 per barrel, hovering near three-week lows.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains as US economic data disappoints and Fed hike bets weaken
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday as weaker-than-expected US economic data pressures the Greenback, while traders closely follow efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of writing, USD/CHF trades around 0.8078, down nearly 0.18% on the day.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average takes another record on Tehran's terms
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 54,500 on Wednesday, 0.76% higher and at a fresh record, roughly 1,400 points above the high it set in early July.

item.title: Japanese Yen consolidates as traders weigh weak US data, market sentiment
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 157.65 on Wednesday at the time of writing, little changed on the day, as weakness in the US Dollar (USD) is offset by investors' cautious stance toward the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: US Dollar slips as ADP collapse offsets hot services
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the performance of the US Dollar (USD) against a basket of six major currencies, trades modestly lower near 99.80 on Wednesday, shedding around 0.15% after a stagflationary batch of United States (US) data.

item.title: British Pound rises as soft ADP jobs report weighs on Dollar, NFP looms
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) advances some 0.12% on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) registers back-to-back days of losses, after US jobs data was softer than expected, even though business activity in the services sector continues to expand solidly. The GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3467.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Daily momentum improves, but weekly outlook stays bearish
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) jumps more than 4% on Wednesday as weaker-than-expected US ADP employment data and easing energy-driven inflation prompt traders to scale back expectations for Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $62.30, near its highest level in a month.

item.title: Euro steadies against Japanese Yen as Eurozone PMIs beat forecasts
item.description: EUR/JPY trades broadly flat near 181.94 on Wednesday, up a marginal 0.01% as the cross pauses after a steady four-session recovery.

item.title: Australian Dollar climbs as softer US data, improving risk sentiment weigh on USD
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7060 on Wednesday at the time of writing, up 0.20% on the day. The pair benefits from broad-based US Dollar (USD) weakness as investors react to softer-than-expected US economic data and improved risk sentiment driven by the latest geopolitical developments.

item.title: Euro: Recovery holds within 1.15–1.16 band against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret describe the Euro (EUR) as steady in the mid-to-lower 1.15 area, trading close to fair value based on 2-year US–Germany spreads. Fundamentals and sentiment are seen as constructive, underpinning EUR recovery since early Q3.

item.title: US Dollar: Limited downside on softer payrolls – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect only modest US Dollar (USD) weakness if July payrolls or the unemployment rate disappoint.

item.title: US Treasury lifts Iran sanctions as deal hopes gain momentum
item.description: On Wednesday, the US removed Iran-related sanctions, according to the US Treasury Department’s website. The US Treasury lifted sanctions imposed on two aircraft linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard ‌Corps (IRGC) and three airlines.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Flows support carry resilience – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes Brazilian portfolio inflows are near post-COVID highs ahead of the Selic decision, with strong demand for equities and government bonds.

item.title: Gold tops $4,200 on softer US labour data as Fed outlook turns less hawkish
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) jumps more than 3.50% on Wednesday as weaker-than-expected US labour market data pressures the US Dollar (USD), while lower Oil prices on hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz ease inflation concerns and weaken expectations for Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes.

item.title: Euro edges higher as weak US labor data, lower Oil prices temper Fed hike bets
item.description: EUR/USD trades modestly higher on Wednesday as weaker-than-expected US labor market data and easing energy-driven inflation risks temper Federal Reserve (Fed) rate-hike expectations and weigh on the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Breaking: ISM Services PMI came in at 54.1 in July
item.description: Fresh data from the Institute for Supply Management (ISM) showed the Services PMI improving a tad to 54.1 in July from 54 in the previous month, coming in short of expectations at 54.5 and signaling some marginal pickup of momentum in the sector.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Labor slack tempers strong jobs data – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the New Zealand Dollar and local yields slumped after strong Q2 employment and wage gains were offset by rising labor supply and higher unemployment.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI seen defending 97 band onshore – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kunal Kundu and Galvin Chia judge the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) August policy outcome as neutral for the Indian Rupee (INR). They highlight fewer comments on INR and flows, but recall Governor Malhotra’s view that INR is not undervalued.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention drop seen capped near 153 – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists see the recent intervention-driven USD/JPY decline as cyclical rather than regime-changing. They expect December as the more likely timing for the next Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike and doubt sustained joint US‑Japan intervention support.
